RewardsCompetitionsNewslettersWeather ForecastWorldElon Musk says SpaceX was behind Starlink restriction that disrupted Ukraine’s defences Ukraine president Volodymyr Zelenskiy says country’s access to Starlink and Starshield satellite links has been fully restoredA residential house destroyed in a Russian missile strike in Kyiv. Photograph: Efrem Lukatsky/AP Susie Blann and Elise Morton, Associated PressSat Oct 24 2026 - 22:30 • 3 MIN READElon Musk has said his company SpaceX had throttled the Starlink satellite internet service in Ukraine, disrupting operations that the country relies on to defend itself against Russia.

Musk’s admission on social media came after Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskiy said that Ukraine’s access to Starlink and Starshield satellite links has been restored to the speeds it had before restrictions that disrupted frontline operations for more than a week.

Questions have persisted since last week about who ordered the interruptions to the Musk-made satellite internet system that Kyiv has relied on for years to counter Moscow’s attacks.

“The speeds are now where they need to be,” Zelensky wrote on X, adding that restoration began on Friday night and were sufficient by Saturday morning, improving frontline logistics and defence against Russian jet-powered Shahed drones.

After Ukraine said the services had been restored, Musk spoke out on the speed restrictions that began last week. In a post on Saturday on X, Musk acknowledged that his company SpaceX had throttled the Starlink satellite internet service.

“Using Starlink, a civilian commercial service, for offensive drone strikes to kill people has never been allowed, nor should it be,” Musk wrote.

“Ukraine military violated Starlink terms of service and used it for offensive drone strikes to kill people. That loophole was closed last week.”

But he maintained that the US government controlled whatever changes happened with Starshield, the military-grade version of Starlink that is the backbone of Ukraine’s drone operations and communication.

He also defended the role of SpaceX in bolstering Ukraine’s defences since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

Restrictions imposed last week on Starshield alarmed the country’s military and government officials, with commanders reporting lost drones and disrupted missions.

The restoration follows a new US diplomatic push to end the war.

Russia agreed on Wednesday to resume three-way negotiations with Washington and Kyiv next month.

On Friday, Kyiv and Moscow also agreed to a localised ceasefire brokered by US first lady Melania Trump around Oleshky, a war-ravaged, Russian-occupied town in Ukraine’s southern Kherson region.

[ Russia and Ukraine agree to local ceasefire in Oleshky amid deepening humanitarian crisisOpens in new window ]

The episode added to tensions between Kyiv and Washington, a relationship already strained by president Donald Trump’s reported deal with Moscow on Russian diesel imports, which Ukraine viewed as a betrayal.

Ukraine’s defence minister Yevhenii Khmara credited “direct dialogue” and Zelenskiy’s diplomacy with Washington, adding that the outcome mattered most “for our front, for the military, the work of drones, logistics and communications”.

Trump has maintained that he did not make the call, while also saying Musk should not be blamed.

Vice president JD Vance has hinted at White House co-ordination with Musk, while US secretary of state Marco Rubio and defence secretary Pete Hegseth have denied any administration involvement.

Meanwhile, a man was killed and two others wounded in a missile attack on the city of Lozova in Ukraine’s Kharkiv region, local officials said on Saturday.

Moscow-installed authorities in cities across Russian-occupied Crimea reported power blackouts on Saturday following overnight Ukrainian attacks.

Ukraine’s General Staff said on Saturday that its forces hit a chemical plant in the Russian city of Tolyatti, which produces materials used in rocket fuel.

Tolyatti mayor Ilya Sukhikh said the overnight attack damaged industrial facilities in the city.

Ukrainian forces also hit an electronics plant in the city of Oryol, Ukraine’s General Staff confirmed on Saturday.

Local officials in Oryol said on Saturday that three people were killed in Friday’s attack.

The General Staff said the plant makes components for the cruise and ballistic missiles Russia fires at Ukrainian cities.

Ukrainian drones also reached Russia’s Omsk region in western Siberia, more than 2,000km  from the border with Ukraine.

Omsk regional governor Vitaly Khotsenko said drones “reached a northern industrial hub”.

Online retailer Ozon said on Saturday that its logistics centre in Omsk has been attacked by a drone, but there were no casualties.
